title: Selecting and filtering rows
summary: Boolean masks, combining conditions with & | ~, isin, between, string matching, and .loc[rows, columns].
hints: A comparison on a column gives a boolean Series, a *mask*: `df["salary"] > threshold`. Indexing with it keeps the rows where it is True: `df[df["salary"] > threshold]`. `in_departments`: `df[df["dept"].isin(depts)]`.

Combine masks with `&` (and), `|` (or) and `~` (not), and put each comparison in parentheses: `(df["dept"] == "Engineering") & (df["age"] < age)`. Python's `and`/`or` do not work on Series. Then `.loc[mask, ["name", "age"]]` picks the columns, and `.reset_index(drop=True)` renumbers the rows.

`names_containing`: `df.loc[df["name"].str.contains(text, case=False, regex=False), "name"].tolist()`. `salary_band`: `df["salary"].between(low, high)` is inclusive on both ends. `max_salary_in`: `int(df.loc[df["city"] == city, "salary"].max())`.
